summary: In August 1951 hundreds of people in the French town of Pont-Saint-Esprit fell ill and hallucinated after eating bread; officials blamed ergot, while later research alleged a CIA LSD experiment.

evidence.note: story opens in the town in the early 1950s; outbreak begins mid-August
toll: roughly 300 to 500 affected, about 50 severe, four deaths
official investigation blames one baker's rye flour and ergot; baker and miller arrested
Albarelli's book on Frank Olson's death and his claim of a CIA LSD field test
1949 Edgewood Arsenal report urging LSD field experiments
CIA memo on a Sandoz official saying the cause was an LSD-like compound, not ergot
aside on CIA airborne LSD dosing in New York City
1975 Rockefeller Commission and its link to the buried Olson file
Gottlieb destroys LSD program records in 1973
historian Kaplan's objections to the CIA theory, then rebuttals

notes: It Could Happen Here episode republished in the BtB feed, so format is crossover; Garrison Davis narrates with Robert Evans. The transcript drops the year digits; 1951 is the well-documented date. covered_span ends at the 1975 Rockefeller Commission; the 2008-2009 books by Kaplan and Albarelli are treated as reinterpretation and set reaches_present instead.
